name: Bigtha
title: Hoffman at the Court of King Ahasuerus
summary: Bigtha (also known as Bigthan) was one of two court officials (eunuchs) who served as doorkeepers at the court of King Ahasuerus in Persia. He and his co-conspirator Teresh plotted to lay hands on King Ahasuerus, but the plot was uncovered by Mordecai. This event played a crucial role in the Book of Esther, as it later led to Mordecai's elevation.

keyEvents.title: Service as Doorkeeper
keyEvents.description: Bigtha served as one of the king's court officials and doorkeepers at King Ahasuerus' palace in Susa.

keyEvents.title: The Conspiracy Against the King
keyEvents.description: Bigtha and Teresh became angry with King Ahasuerus and planned to lay hands on him. The two court officials secretly conspired against the king's life.

keyEvents.title: Mordecai Uncovers the Plot
keyEvents.description: Mordecai learned of the conspiracy and reported it to Queen Esther, who then brought it to the king in Mordecai's name.

keyEvents.title: The Conspiracy Confirmed and Punishment Executed
keyEvents.description: The matter was investigated and found to be true, and both men were hanged on a gallows. The event was recorded in the chronicle in the king's presence.

keyEvents.title: The Event Is Read to the King
keyEvents.description: Later, during a sleepless night, the book of chronicles was read aloud to King Ahasuerus, and he was reminded of Mordecai's merit in exposing Bigtha's conspiracy.

keyEvents.title: Mordecai's Reward Following the Exposure
keyEvents.description: The king's rediscovery of Mordecai's role in exposing the plot led to Mordecai's elevation and helped turn the fate of the Jewish people.
